sanskrit: anena caiva dehena lokāṃs tvam abhipatsyase nirjitaś ca tvayā mṛtyur aiśvaryaṃ ca tavottamam
english: With this very body you shall win the worlds; Death has been conquered by you, and supreme is the sovereignty that is yours.

sanskrit: pañca bhūtāny atikrāntaḥ svavīryāc ca manobhavaḥ gṛhasthadharmeṇānena kāmakrodhau ca te jitau
english: By your own valor you have transcended the five elements and the mind-born one; and by this dharma of the householder both desire and anger have been conquered by you.

sanskrit: sneho rāgaś ca tandrī ca moho drohaś ca kevalaḥ tava śuśrūṣayā rājan rājaputryā vinirjitāḥ
english: Attachment and passion, sloth, delusion, and sheer malice—all these, O king, have been wholly vanquished through the devoted service of your princess-wife.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śuklānāṃ tu sahasreṇa vājināṃ ratham uttamam yuktaṃ pragṛhya bhagavān vyavasāyo jagāma tam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the lord Resolve, taking hold of a most excellent chariot yoked with a thousand white steeds, departed to that place.

sanskrit: mṛtyur ātmā ca lokāś ca jitā bhūtāni pañca ca buddhiḥ kālo mano vyoma kāmakrodhau tathaiva ca
english: Death and the self and the worlds were conquered, and the five elements, intellect, time, mind, and ether, and likewise desire and anger as well.

sanskrit: tasmād gṛhāśramasthasya nānyad daivatam asti vai ṛte 'tithiṃ naravyāghra manasaitad vicāraya
english: Therefore, for one established in the householder's order, there is verily no other deity than the guest, O tiger among men—ponder this in your mind.

sanskrit: atithiḥ pūjito yasya dhyāyate manasā śubham na tat kratuśatenāpi tulyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: When a guest, having been honored, dwells in his mind upon a man's welfare, the wise declare that not even by a hundred sacrifices is its equal attained.

sanskrit: pātraṃ tv atithim āsādya śīlāḍhyaṃ yo na pūjayet sa dattvā sukṛtaṃ tasya kṣapayeta hy anarcitaḥ
english: But whoever, on receiving a worthy guest rich in virtue, fails to honor him—that unhonored guest, by departing, makes away with the host's store of merit.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ putra mayākhyānam anuttamam yathā hi vijito mṛtyur gṛhasthena purābhavat
english: This unsurpassed tale has been told to you by me, my son—how Death was vanquished of old by a householder.

sanskrit: dhanyaṃ yaśasyam āyuṣyam idam ākhyānam uttamam bubhūṣatābhimantavyaṃ sarvaduścaritāpaham
english: This excellent tale brings prosperity, fame, and long life; it should be reflected upon by one who wishes for well-being, for it wipes away all evil conduct.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ kathayed vidvān ahany ahani bhārata sudarśanasya caritaṃ puṇyāṃl lokān avāpnuyāt
english: That learned man who would recite this day after day, O Bhārata—the deeds of Sudarśana—would attain the holy worlds.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brāhmaṇyaṃ yadi duṣprāpaṃ tribhir varṇair narādhipa kathaṃ prāptaṃ mahārāja kṣatriyeṇa mahātmanā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If brahmanhood is hard to attain by the three varṇas, O lord of men, how was it attained, O great king, by a great-souled kṣatriya?

sanskrit: viśvāmitreṇa dharmātman brāhmaṇatvaṃ nararṣabha śrotum icchāmi tattvena tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: By Viśvāmitra, O righteous one, brahmanhood was attained, O bull among men; I wish to hear of this truly—tell it to me, grandsire.

sanskrit: tena hy amitavīryeṇa vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ hataṃ putraśataṃ sadyas tapasā prapitāmaha
english: For by him of boundless valor the hundred sons of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha were slain in an instant by the power of his austerity, O great-grandsire.

sanskrit: yātudhānāś ca bahavo rākṣasās tigmatejasaḥ manyunāviṣṭadehena sṛṣṭāḥ kālāntakopamāḥ
english: And many sorcerers and rākṣasas of fierce energy, like Time the destroyer, were created by him whose body was possessed by wrath.

sanskrit: mahān kuśikavaṃśaś ca brahmarṣiśatasaṃkulaḥ sthāpito naraloke 'smin vidvān brāhmaṇasaṃstutaḥ
english: And the great lineage of Kuśika, thronged with a hundred brahmin-sages, was established in this world of men by the learned one praised among brahmins.

sanskrit: ṛcīkasyātmajaś caiva śunaḥśepo mahātapāḥ vimokṣito mahāsatrāt paśutām abhyupāgataḥ
english: And Śunaḥśepa, the son of Ṛcīka, of great austerity, who had been reduced to the state of a sacrificial victim, was set free from the great sacrifice.

sanskrit: hariścandrakratau devāṃs toṣayitvātmatejasā putratām anusaṃprāpto viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
english: At the sacrifice of Hariścandra, having gratified the gods by his own splendor, he came to be a son of the wise Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: nābhivādayate jyeṣṭhaṃ devarātaṃ narādhipa putrāḥ pañcaśatāś cāpi śaptāḥ śvapacatāṃ gatāḥ
english: When the five hundred sons did not salute their eldest, Devarāta, O lord of men, they were cursed and reduced to the condition of dog-cookers.

sanskrit: triśaṅkur bandhusaṃtyakta ikṣvākuḥ prītipūrvakam avākśirā divaṃ nīto dakṣiṇām āśrito diśam
english: Triśaṅku the Ikṣvāku, forsaken by his kinsmen, was borne lovingly to heaven head-downward, abiding in the southern quarter.

sanskrit: viśvāmitrasya vipulā nadī rājarṣisevitā kauśikīti śivā puṇyā brahmarṣigaṇasevitā
english: The broad river of Viśvāmitra, frequented by royal sages, the auspicious and holy Kauśikī, is resorted to by hosts of brahmin-sages.

sanskrit: tapovighnakarī caiva pañcacūḍā susaṃmatā rambhā nāmāpsarāḥ śāpād yasya śailatvam āgatā
english: And the apsaras named Rambhā of the five tresses, highly esteemed, who came to obstruct his austerity, was by his curse turned into stone.

sanskrit: tathaivāsya bhayād baddhvā vasiṣṭhaḥ salile purā ātmānaṃ majjayām āsa vipāśaḥ punar utthitaḥ
english: And likewise, in fear of him of old, Vasiṣṭha bound himself and plunged into the water, but, his fetters undone, he rose up again.

sanskrit: tadāprabhṛti puṇyā hi vipāśābhūn mahānadī vikhyātā karmaṇā tena vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ
english: From that time onward the holy great river became known as Vipāśā, by reason of that deed of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: vāgbhiś ca bhagavān yena devasenāgragaḥ prabhuḥ stutaḥ prītamanāś cāsīc chāpāc cainam amocayat
english: And by whom the lord Skanda, leader of the host of the gods, was praised with hymns and became glad of heart, and released him from a curse.

sanskrit: dhruvasyauttānapādasya brahmarṣīṇāṃ tathaiva ca madhye jvalati yo nityam udīcīm āśrito diśam
english: And he who blazes ever in the midst of Dhruva, son of Uttānapāda, and of the brahmin-sages, abiding in the northern quarter.

sanskrit: tasyaitāni ca karmāṇi tathānyāni ca kaurava kṣatriyasyety ato jātam idaṃ kautūhalaṃ mama
english: These deeds of his, and others too, O Kaurava—done by a kṣatriya—it is from this that my curiosity has arisen.

sanskrit: kim etad iti tattvena prabrūhi bharatarṣabha dehāntaram anāsādya kathaṃ sa brāhmaṇo 'bhavat
english: What is this? Tell me truly, O bull of the Bharatas: without taking on another body, how did he become a brahmin?

sanskrit: etat tattvena me rājan sarvam ākhyātum arhasi mataṃgasya yathātattvaṃ tathaivaitad bravīhi me
english: All this you ought to recount to me truly, O king; and as the truth of Mataṅga was, so too tell me this.

sanskrit: sthāne mataṃgo brāhmaṇyaṃ nālabhad bharatarṣabha caṇḍālayonau jāto hi kathaṃ brāhmaṇyam āpnuyāt
english: With reason did Mataṅga fail to attain brahmanhood, O bull of the Bharatas; for, born in the womb of a caṇḍāla, how could he attain brahmanhood?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śrūyatāṃ pārtha tattvena viśvāmitro yathā purā brāhmaṇatvaṃ gatas tāta brahmarṣitvaṃ tathaiva ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Let it be heard truly, O Pārtha, how of old Viśvāmitra attained to brahmanhood, my son, and likewise to the state of a brahmin-sage.

sanskrit: bharatasyānvaye caivājamīḍho nāma pārthivaḥ babhūva bharataśreṣṭha yajvā dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: In the lineage of Bharata there was a king named Ajamīḍha, O best of the Bharatas, a performer of sacrifices, foremost among upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: tasya putro mahān āsīj jahnur nāma nareśvaraḥ duhitṛtvam anuprāptā gaṅgā yasya mahātmanaḥ
english: His son was the great lord of men named Jahnu, whose daughter the great-souled Gaṅgā became.

sanskrit: tasyātmajas tulyaguṇaḥ sindhudvīpo mahāyaśāḥ sindhudvīpāc ca rājarṣir balākāśvo mahābalaḥ
english: His son, of equal virtues, was the greatly renowned Sindhudvīpa; and from Sindhudvīpa came the royal sage Balākāśva of great might.

sanskrit: vallabhas tasya tanayaḥ sākṣād dharma ivāparaḥ kuśikas tasya tanayaḥ sahasrākṣasamadyutiḥ
english: His son was Vallabha, like another Dharma made manifest; his son was Kuśika, equal in splendor to the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: kuśikasyātmajaḥ śrīmān gādhir nāma janeśvaraḥ aputraḥ sa mahābāhur vanavāsam udāvasat
english: The illustrious son of Kuśika was the lord of men named Gādhi; that mighty-armed one, being without a son, went to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: kanyā jajñe sutā tasya vane nivasataḥ sataḥ nāmnā satyavatī nāma rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi
english: To him as he dwelt in the forest a daughter was born, a maiden named Satyavatī, unmatched in beauty upon the earth.

sanskrit: tāṃ vavre bhārgavaḥ śrīmāṃś cyavanasyātmajaḥ prabhuḥ ṛcīka iti vikhyāto vipule tapasi sthitaḥ
english: Her the illustrious lord of the Bhṛgu line, the son of Cyavana, renowned as Ṛcīka, established in vast austerity, sought in marriage.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ na pradadau tasmai ṛcīkāya mahātmane daridra iti matvā vai gādhiḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: But Gādhi, crusher of foes, did not give her to that great-souled Ṛcīka, deeming him to be poor.

sanskrit: pratyākhyāya punar yāntam abravīd rājasattamaḥ śulkaṃ pradīyatāṃ mahyaṃ tato vetsyasi me sutām
english: Having refused him, that best of kings said to him as he was departing again: "Let a bride-price be given to me; then shall you wed my daughter."

sanskrit: ṛcīka uvāca kiṃ prayacchāmi rājendra tubhyaṃ śulkam ahaṃ nṛpa duhitur brūhy asaṃsakto mātrābhūt te vicāraṇā
english: Ṛcīka said: What bride-price shall I give to you, O lord of kings, O sovereign, for your daughter? Speak freely; let there be no hesitation of reckoning in you.

sanskrit: gādhir uvāca candraraśmiprakāśānāṃ hayānāṃ vātaraṃhasām ekataḥ śyāmakarṇānāṃ sahasraṃ dehi bhārgava
english: Gādhi said: Of horses bright as the moon's rays, swift as the wind, dark in one ear, give me a thousand, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa bhṛguśārdūlaś cyavanasyātmajaḥ prabhuḥ abravīd varuṇaṃ devam ādityaṃ patim ambhasām
english: Bhīṣma said: Then that tiger of the Bhṛgus, the lord, son of Cyavana, addressed the god Varuṇa, the Āditya, lord of the waters:

sanskrit: ekataḥ śyāmakarṇānāṃ hayānāṃ candravarcasām sahasraṃ vātavegānāṃ bhikṣe tvāṃ devasattama
english: "Of horses dark in one ear, with the luster of the moon, swift as the wind—a thousand I beg of you, O best of the gods."

sanskrit: tatheti varuṇo deva ādityo bhṛgusattamam uvāca yatra te chandas tatrotthāsyanti vājinaḥ
english: "So be it," said the god Varuṇa, the Āditya, to that best of the Bhṛgus: "Wherever you desire, there shall the steeds arise."

sanskrit: dhyātamātre ṛcīkena hayānāṃ candravarcasām gaṅgājalāt samuttasthau sahasraṃ vipulaujasām
english: No sooner had Ṛcīka meditated upon them than a thousand horses with the luster of the moon, of vast vigor, rose up from the waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: adūre kanyakubjasya gaṅgāyās tīram uttamam aśvatīrthaṃ tad adyāpi mānavāḥ paricakṣate
english: That excellent bank of the Gaṅgā, not far from Kānyakubja, men call even to this day the Ford of Horses.

sanskrit: tat tadā gādhaye tāta sahasraṃ vājināṃ śubham ṛcīkaḥ pradadau prītaḥ śulkārthaṃ japatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then, my son, Ṛcīka, foremost among those who murmur prayers, gladly gave that fair thousand of horses to Gādhi as the bride-price.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vismito rājā gādhiḥ śāpabhayena ca dadau tāṃ samalaṃkṛtya kanyāṃ bhṛgusutāya vai
english: Then king Gādhi, astonished and also fearful of a curse, adorned the maiden and gave her to the son of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: jagrāha pāṇiṃ vidhinā tasya brahmarṣisattamaḥ sā ca taṃ patim āsādya paraṃ harṣam avāpa ha
english: That best of brahmin-sages took her hand according to the rite, and she, having gained him for her husband, attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: sa tutoṣa ca viprarṣis tasyā vṛttena bhārata chandayām āsa caivaināṃ vareṇa varavarṇinīm
english: And the brahmin-sage was well pleased with her conduct, O Bhārata, and offered that fair-complexioned woman the granting of a boon.

sanskrit: mātre tat sarvam ācakhyau sā kanyā rājasattamam atha tām abravīn mātā sutāṃ kiṃ cid avāṅmukhīm
english: That maiden told all of it to her mother, O best of kings; then the mother said to her daughter, whose face was somewhat downcast:

sanskrit: mamāpi putri bhartā te prasādaṃ kartum arhati apatyasya pradānena samarthaḥ sa mahātapāḥ
english: "To me also, my daughter, your husband ought to show favor; that one of great austerity is able to grant offspring."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā tvaritaṃ gatvā tat sarvaṃ pratyavedayat mātuś cikīrṣitaṃ rājann ṛcīkas tām athābravīt
english: Then she went in haste and reported it all—what her mother wished to be done, O king—and Ṛcīka thereupon said to her:

sanskrit: guṇavantam apatyaṃ vai tvaṃ ca sā janayiṣyathaḥ jananyās tava kalyāṇi mā bhūd vai praṇayo 'nyathā
english: "You and she shall each bring forth virtuous offspring, O blessed one; let not the wish of your mother turn out otherwise."

sanskrit: tava caiva guṇaślāghī putra utpatsyate śubhe asmadvaṃśakaraḥ śrīmāṃs tava bhrātā ca vaṃśakṛt
english: "And to you, O fair one, shall be born a son praised for his virtues, illustrious, the continuer of our line; and your brother too shall be the founder of a line."

sanskrit: ṛtusnātā ca sāśvatthaṃ tvaṃ ca vṛkṣam udumbaram pariṣvajethāḥ kalyāṇi tata iṣṭam avāpsyathaḥ
english: "And bathed after your season, she shall embrace an aśvattha tree and you an udumbara tree, O blessed one; thereby you both shall obtain what you desire."

sanskrit: carudvayam idaṃ caiva mantrapūtaṃ śucismite tvaṃ ca sā copayuñjīthāṃ tataḥ putrāv avāpsyathaḥ
english: "And these two oblations of rice, hallowed by sacred formulas, O you of bright smile—you and she shall partake of them, and then you both shall obtain sons."

sanskrit: tataḥ satyavatī hṛṣṭā mātaraṃ pratyabhāṣata yad ṛcīkena kathitaṃ tac cācakhyau carudvayam
english: Then Satyavatī, gladdened, spoke in reply to her mother and told her what Ṛcīka had said, and of the two oblations.

sanskrit: tām uvāca tato mātā sutāṃ satyavatīṃ tadā putri mūrdhnā prapannāyāḥ kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama
english: Then the mother spoke thus to her daughter Satyavatī: "My daughter, since I take refuge with bowed head, do as I bid you."

sanskrit: bhartrā ya eṣa dattas te carur mantrapuraskṛtaḥ etaṃ prayaccha mahyaṃ tvaṃ madīyaṃ tvaṃ gṛhāṇa ca
english: "This oblation, hallowed with sacred formulas, which has been given to you by your husband—give it to me, and take you mine."

sanskrit: vyatyāsaṃ vṛkṣayoś cāpi karavāva śucismite yadi pramāṇaṃ vacanaṃ mama mātur anindite
english: "And let us two also make an exchange of the trees, O you of bright smile, if the word of your mother is of any authority, O blameless one."

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ bhagavatā cātra kṛtam evaṃ bhaviṣyati tato me tvaccarau bhāvaḥ pādape ca sumadhyame kathaṃ viśiṣṭo bhrātā te bhaved ity eva cintaya
english: "Surely whatever the holy one has appointed in this matter shall come to pass; therefore my desire is set upon your oblation and upon your tree, O slender-waisted one. Consider only thus: how may your brother prove the more excellent."

sanskrit: tathā ca kṛtavatyau te mātā satyavatī ca sā atha garbhāv anuprāpte ubhe te vai yudhiṣṭhira
english: And thus the mother and Satyavatī both did, and then both of them conceived, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā garbham anuprāptāṃ bhāryāṃ sa ca mahān ṛṣiḥ uvāca tāṃ satyavatīṃ durmanā bhṛgusattamaḥ
english: And that great sage, the best of the Bhṛgus, seeing his wife with child, said to Satyavatī, troubled in mind:

sanskrit: vyatyāsenopayuktas te carur vyaktaṃ bhaviṣyati vyatyāsaḥ pādape cāpi suvyaktaṃ te kṛtaḥ śubhe
english: "Plainly the oblation has been partaken of by you in exchange, and plainly an exchange has been made by you with regard to the tree as well, O fair one."

sanskrit: mayā hi viśvaṃ yad brahma tvaccarau saṃniveśitam kṣatravīryaṃ ca sakalaṃ carau tasyā niveśitam
english: "For all the brahmin power I had placed in your oblation, and the whole of the kṣatriya might I had placed in hers."

sanskrit: trilokavikhyātaguṇaṃ tvaṃ vipraṃ janayiṣyasi sā ca kṣatraṃ viśiṣṭaṃ vai tata etat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "You were to bring forth a brahmin of virtues renowned throughout the three worlds, and she a kṣatriya of surpassing kind; for this end was this done by me."

sanskrit: vyatyāsas tu kṛto yasmāt tvayā mātrā tathaiva ca tasmāt sā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ mātā te janayiṣyati
english: "But since the exchange has been made by you and likewise by your mother, therefore your mother shall bring forth the best of brahmins."

sanskrit: kṣatriyaṃ tūgrakarmāṇaṃ tvaṃ bhadre janayiṣyasi na hi te tat kṛtaṃ sādhu mātṛsnehena bhāmini
english: "But you, O gentle one, shall bring forth a kṣatriya of fierce deeds; for what you did out of love for your mother was not well done, O proud lady."

sanskrit: sā śrutvā śokasaṃtaptā papāta varavarṇinī bhūmau satyavatī rājaṃś chinneva rucirā latā
english: Hearing this, the fair-complexioned Satyavatī, scorched with grief, fell to the ground, O king, like a lovely creeper cut through.

sanskrit: pratilabhya ca sā saṃjñāṃ śirasā praṇipatya ca uvāca bhāryā bhartāraṃ gādheyī brāhmaṇarṣabham
english: And regaining her senses and bowing down with her head, the wife, the daughter of Gādhi, said to her husband, that bull among brahmins:

sanskrit: prasādayantyāṃ bhāryāyāṃ mayi brahmavidāṃ vara prasādaṃ kuru viprarṣe na me syāt kṣatriyaḥ sutaḥ
english: "As your wife implores you, O best of the knowers of Brahman, show favor, O brahmin-sage: let no kṣatriya be my son."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ mamograkarmā vai pautro bhavitum arhati na tu me syāt suto brahmann eṣa me dīyatāṃ varaḥ
english: "Let my grandson, if you will, be one of fierce deeds, but let not my son be such, O brahmin: let this boon be granted to me."

sanskrit: evam astv iti hovāca svāṃ bhāryāṃ sumahātapāḥ tataḥ sā janayām āsa jamadagniṃ sutaṃ śubham
english: "So be it," said the one of mighty austerity to his wife; and then she brought forth a fair son, Jamadagni.

sanskrit: viśvāmitraṃ cājanayad gādher bhāryā yaśasvinī ṛṣeḥ prabhāvād rājendra brahmarṣiṃ brahmavādinam
english: And the renowned wife of Gādhi brought forth Viśvāmitra, by the power of the sage, O lord of kings—a brahmin-sage, an expounder of Brahman.

sanskrit: tato brāhmaṇatāṃ yāto viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ kṣatriyaḥ so 'py atha tathā brahmavaṃśasya kārakaḥ
english: Thus Viśvāmitra of great austerity, though a kṣatriya, attained to brahmanhood, and so became the founder of a brahmin lineage.

sanskrit: tasya putrā mahātmāno brahmavaṃśavivardhanāḥ tapasvino brahmavido gotrakartāra eva ca
english: His sons were great-souled, increasers of the brahmin line, ascetics, knowers of Brahman, and founders of gotras as well.

sanskrit: madhucchandaś ca bhagavān devarātaś ca vīryavān akṣīṇaś ca śakuntaś ca babhruḥ kālapathas tathā
english: The lord Madhucchandas, and the valiant Devarāta, and Akṣīṇa, and Śakunta, Babhru, and Kālapatha likewise;

sanskrit: yājñavalkyaś ca vikhyātas tathā sthūṇo mahāvrataḥ ulūko yamadūtaś ca tatharṣiḥ saindhavāyanaḥ
english: And the renowned Yājñavalkya, and Sthūṇa of great vows, Ulūka and Yamadūta, and likewise the sage Saindhavāyana.
